title: Enterprise VPC risk and value narrative (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This brief is a compact narrative for GTM — short reads for sales, solutions engineering, and AE prep. Focus: regulated workloads (finance, healthcare, gov), technical language around a customer-managed management plane, and concise rebuttals to common buyer concerns. Use as a scripting reference and to inform collateral updates.

Top-level positioning (one-liner):
Redwood Private gives regulated teams the predictability of a hosted inference product with a customer-owned management plane and auditable controls so sensitive workloads run with cloud-grade performance and enterprise controls.

Target personas and what they care about:
- CTO / Head of Platform: control, integration with existing infra, vendor lock-in risk, upgrade path.
- CISO / Security Lead: data residency, KMS/HSM, least privilege, attestation, pen test history.
- Compliance / Audit Owner: audit trails, evidence for regulators, SOC/ISO equivalence, data retention controls.
- ML/Infra Lead: model consistency, latency SLOs, KV cache security, model rollouts and rollback mechanics.
- Procurement / Legal: contract controls, liability boundaries, support SLAs, termination & data return.

Core messages (3–4 pillars):
1) Customer ownership and separation: the management plane can be deployed into the customer VPC or on-prem network; configuration metadata and control signals are customer-managed. Minimal metadata crosses outbound-only control channels when requested by the customer. This reduces third-party access surface while preserving our deployment automation.
2) Auditability and evidence: built-in audit logs, signed config diffs, and crypto-backed artifact verification make it feasible to produce regulator-grade evidence for who changed model routing, rollouts, and keys.
3) Predictable economics with operational safeguards: reserved capacity patterns and transparent cost-breakdowns per route/model let finance trade latency for unit cost. We provide pre-approved batching & caching configurations that meet SLOs for regulated latency-sensitive flows.
4) Safe fallback and graceful degradation: in failure modes Redwood Private can route to pre-approved on-prem model variants or block external fallbacks so critical flows never leak data.

Technical language to use (concise):
- Management plane = customer-managed control interface (can run in VPC).
- Data path isolation = inference traffic never crosses the control plane boundary; KV caches are local by default.
- Artifact signing = container/model artifacts signed with customer or customer-trusted keys.
- HSM/KMS integration = bring-your-own-key for model + log encryption.
- Non-privileged operators = role-based access with short-lived certs and attested agent identity.

Competitive differentiation (short):
- Public cloud managed endpoints: lower friction but persistent provider access and inconsistent multi-region audit artifacts.
- Pure self-build inference runtimes: full control but long time-to-production, no packaged observability, and unsupported SLOs.
- Other inference vendors: often require either full vendor control of orchestration or lack enterprise-graded audit/evidence. Redwood Private occupies the sweet spot: packaged runtime + customer-owned control plane with documented evidence for auditors.

Common buyer objections and tight rebuttals (quick scripts):
1) Objection: "We can't let a vendor host the control plane or have keys."
   Rebuttal: "Understood — Redwood Private supports a customer-run management plane in your VPC and BYOK via your HSM. Our control messages are outbound-only by default and artifacts are signed against your key material so the vendor has no covert access. We can run the management control in an air-gapped subnet where only specific operator CIDRs have access."
2) Objection: "We need full air-gap for high-regulation workloads."
   Rebuttal: "We have a validated on-prem distribution that runs entirely inside your network. In that mode telemetry is optional, and we provide an encrypted offline sync package for updates and signed artifact ingestion. SEs can walk through the exact offline patch process during a PoC."
3) Objection: "This looks expensive compared to hosted endpoints."
   Rebuttal: "Upfront reserved capacity and predictable bundling reduces per-token volatility; plus our Optimize recommendations typically reduce token spend by 25–40% for latency-sensitive throughput workloads. We can run a 30-day workload audit to show net-dollar impact for your traffic pattern."
4) Objection: "We have an internal MLOps team; why buy Redwood?"
   Rebuttal: "Redwood is not a rip-and-replace — it provides a hardened, GPU-optimized serving runtime, audit trails, and rollout tooling your MLOps team can integrate with. Most customers keep their CI/CD/validation flows and adopt Redwood to reduce operational toil and achieve SLOs without custom kernel tuning."

Field playbook (recommended short sequence):
- 0–5 min elevator: quick value prop + confirm constraints (BYOK? air-gap? audit cadence?)
- 15–30 min technical review: show network diagrams (control plane in VPC vs on-prem), discuss artifact signing, KMS flows, and rollback policies. Ask for existing audit requirements and incident playbooks.
- PoC scope: 2-week POC with a single regulated flow (eg: PII-extraction pipeline), customer-owned KMS, telemetry disabled, and a rollback/kill-switch test.
- Success criteria: end-to-end latency under agreed SLO, end-to-end audit evidence for 5 operations, cost projection validated against 30 days of traffic.

Conversation tactics and language dos/don'ts:
- Do: use concrete artifacts (sample signed audit logs, diagram of management plane placement) when possible.
- Do: ask for the regulator name/standard early (e.g., FCA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) and map requirements to product features (retention windows, key escrow rules).
- Don't: overpromise on air-gap timelines — be explicit about offline patch cadence and validation windows.
- Don't: use 'control plane lock-in' as a scare tactic; instead, emphasize signed artifacts and exportable configs.

Pre-baked collateral suggestions (priority order):
1) One-pager: 'Management plane placement options' with network diagrams and checkbox for audit needs.
2) Checklist: 'Pre-POC compliance checklist' for CISO and audit teams.
3) Technical appendix: detailed sequence diagrams for model rollouts, signed artifact ingestion, and HSM flows.
4) Customer case stub: anonymized vignettes for finance and healthcare showing audit readiness and latency outcomes.

Next steps for GTM updates (owner assignments):
- Sales enablement deck update: include 2 new slides and 1 appendix (owner: Priya Patel).
- SE lab runbook: create a step-by-step PoC guide for air-gapped and BYOK (owner: Ethan Wright).
- Legal variable: create contract addendum templates for on-prem/air-gapped deployments and data-return clauses (owner: Liam O'Connor).

Open questions for product/security: 
- Exact default telemetry opt-in/opt-out UX for Private on first install.
- SLA language for on-prem agent availability and support response that legal can commit to.
- Template wording for signed artifact verification that auditors accept as evidence.

Appendix: sample 60-second pitch (for executives)
"Many regulated teams face a tradeoff: keep everything internal and accept slow, bespoke ML ops, or adopt hosted inference and exchange control. Redwood Private removes that tradeoff. We ship a high-performance inference runtime that lives where you want it and a management layer you control. That means demonstrable audit trails, BYOK, and predictable costs — so your security and finance teams get evidence and predictability, and your engineers get inference that scales."

Notes on tone: keep messaging concrete and technical when talking to infra and compliance buyers; for execs keep it benefits-first with clear mitigation of regulatory risk.

Revision history: initial draft 2025-11-03 by Maya Chen; updated rebuttals and PoC scope 2026-02-28.
